title: Ultra-portable X-rays read by CAD4TB screened 94,694 people for tuberculosis in eight Nigerian states in 2022, and the program diagnosed 2,337 cases
summary: In 2022, CAD4TB version 7 scored ultra-portable chest X-rays of 94,694 people in eight Nigerian states, alongside symptom screening: 2,337 TB cases diagnosed, 97% treated.
account: KNCV Tuberculosis Foundation Nigeria and the Institute of Human Virology Nigeria, funded by the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID), deployed ten ultra-portable digital X-ray units. The work was part of the Stop TB Partnership's Introducing New Tools Project. From January to September 2022, the units ran CAD4TB version 7, with a threshold score of 50, for community active case finding in eight states: Katsina, Kano, Nasarawa, Benue, Delta, Cross River, Osun and Oyo. Under a parallel algorithm, every client had both symptom and chest X-ray screening. Anyone positive on either screen, including anyone with a CAD4TB score of 50 or above, was classified as presumptive tuberculosis (TB). These clients were sent for Xpert testing, clinical assessment or both. The program screened 94,694 people aged four and over and identified 10,236 presumptive cases. It diagnosed 2,337 TB cases: 920 bacteriologically confirmed, 1,386 clinically diagnosed and 31 rifampicin-resistant. Of those diagnosed, 1,614 (69.1%) scored 50 or above and 723 (30.9%) scored below 50. The authors report that 97.3% started treatment and that the average number needed to screen was 38. The paper's tables tally 2,481 diagnoses (986 bacteriologically confirmed, 1,466 clinically diagnosed, 29 rifampicin-resistant) with 2,414 (97.3%) started on treatment. The authors derive the number needed to screen of 38 from that tally, and their text gives 2,337 diagnoses. A companion six-state analysis reported 85,910 screened, 1,915 diagnosed and 1,869 treated. It gives a number needed to screen of 44.9 for the portable X-ray system, against 49.0 to 388.5 for KNCV Nigeria's other main case-finding strategies. The published studies of the ten ultra-portable units all come from KNCV Nigeria, the Institute of Human Virology Nigeria or the national TB program, with USAID funding. KNCV Nigeria's 2025 annual report says that the IMPACT project added 266 portable digital X-ray units with AI in 2025, completing 390 units across all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. The report says that over 780,000 people were screened with these units from January to September 2025 and that over 23,000 TB cases were diagnosed.

ai_role.statement: A parallel algorithm classified anyone positive on symptom screening or with a CAD4TB score of 50 or above as presumptive TB. They went for Xpert testing and/or clinical assessment, so the AI score was one of two gates to testing, not the sole gate. Of the 2,337 diagnosed, 1,614 (69.1%) scored 50 or above and 723 (30.9%) scored below 50. The TB yield also depends on X-ray reach, Xpert availability and treatment linkage. Both papers are authored by implementing organizations (KNCV Nigeria, IHVN, USAID, NTBLCP), not the vendor.

fields.summary: In 2022, CAD4TB version 7 scored ultra-portable chest X-rays of 94,694 people in eight Nigerian states, alongside symptom screening: 2,337 TB cases diagnosed, 97% treated.
fields.account: KNCV Tuberculosis Foundation Nigeria and the Institute of Human Virology Nigeria, funded by the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID), deployed ten ultra-portable digital X-ray units. The work was part of the Stop TB Partnership's Introducing New Tools Project. From January to September 2022, the units ran CAD4TB version 7, with a threshold score of 50, for community active case finding in eight states: Katsina, Kano, Nasarawa, Benue, Delta, Cross River, Osun and Oyo. Under a parallel algorithm, every client had both symptom and chest X-ray screening. Anyone positive on either screen, including anyone with a CAD4TB score of 50 or above, was classified as presumptive tuberculosis (TB). These clients were sent for Xpert testing, clinical assessment or both. The program screened 94,694 people aged four and over and identified 10,236 presumptive cases. It diagnosed 2,337 TB cases: 920 bacteriologically confirmed, 1,386 clinically diagnosed and 31 rifampicin-resistant. Of those diagnosed, 1,614 (69.1%) scored 50 or above and 723 (30.9%) scored below 50. The authors report that 97.3% started treatment and that the average number needed to screen was 38. The paper's tables tally 2,481 diagnoses (986 bacteriologically confirmed, 1,466 clinically diagnosed, 29 rifampicin-resistant) with 2,414 (97.3%) started on treatment. The authors derive the number needed to screen of 38 from that tally, and their text gives 2,337 diagnoses. A companion six-state analysis reported 85,910 screened, 1,915 diagnosed and 1,869 treated. It gives a number needed to screen of 44.9 for the portable X-ray system, against 49.0 to 388.5 for KNCV Nigeria's other main case-finding strategies. The published studies of the ten ultra-portable units all come from KNCV Nigeria, the Institute of Human Virology Nigeria or the national TB program, with USAID funding. KNCV Nigeria's 2025 annual report says that the IMPACT project added 266 portable digital X-ray units with AI in 2025, completing 390 units across all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. The report says that over 780,000 people were screened with these units from January to September 2025 and that over 23,000 TB cases were diagnosed.
